meta.title: Lesson 5 data: capacity factors, the year profiles' targets, the solar day and the illustrative turbine

meta.about: The wind and solar shapes in town_year.json are each divided by their own 2025 maximum hour, so their mean is NOT a capacity factor (wind 0.528, solar 0.235). The lesson turns them into a plant's output with the shared helper LX.townProfile (assets/learn/components/profiles.js), method "power", to the annual targets in the shared cf_targets.json (EIA Table 6.07.B, 2025), with each month first brought to the 2025 U.S. monthly capacity factor (the helper's monthlyCF option; the values are in cf_targets.json, monthly). Night-time solar telemetry is already zero in town_year.json (the town data build step). Nuclear runs at full size except for one illustrative refuelling outage (nuclear). Why "power": the best hours reach the plant's size, so the year view shows output against nameplate.

year.about: town_year.json: index i is the hour ending at start_utc + i (UTC). start_utc is 2025-01-01T07:00, so index 0 is the hour 00:00-01:00 Central Standard Time on 1 January and the 8,760 hours make 365 whole local days (standard time, UTC-6, all year).

nuclear.about: Illustrative: the plant runs at full size all year except one spring refuelling outage of 780 hours (32.5 days, from 25 March), so that the year's capacity factor is (8760 - 780) / 8760 = 91.1%, the 2025 U.S. average. EIA: plants refuel every 18 to 24 months, mostly in spring and fall; the average planned outage in 2022 lasted 38 days.

day.about: An illustrative solar day based on SPP observations: the 100 MW solar farm's hourly output on the lesson-0 day, Central daylight time (UTC-5), rounded to whole MW. It is the year profile's day (SPP's 2025 shape, reshaped month by month to the U.S. capacity factors) as built from town_year.json (whose solar is zero when the sun is below the horizon at SPP's centre), stored here so the page's static table, the steps and the explain layer state the same 24 numbers. The lesson's test checks it against the year profile hour by hour (within 1 MW).

turbine.about: Illustrative onshore turbine with a clean power curve: below the rated speed the output follows the cube law, P = rated x (v / ratedSpeed)^3; from the rated speed to the cut-out speed it holds its rated power; outside [cutIn, cutOut] it makes nothing. With a 100 m rotor and air at 1.225 kg/m3 this is a power coefficient of 0.36 at the rated speed, below the Betz limit 16/27.

apply.about: Step 8: Prairie Town's wind farm (town.json fleet.wind.mw) at the 2025 U.S. wind capacity factor.

measured.about: Go deeper (Modeler): a measured power curve. Bins of 0.5 m/s from the report's Table 6, transcribed by hand: [normalised wind speed m/s, average power kW, number of 10-minute data sets, Category A standard uncertainty kW]. NREL ran the test to the IEC 61400-12-1 power-performance standard with two stated exceptions, for which it added uncertainty: no site calibration although the site failed the terrain assessment, and a hub-height anemometer on a side boom rather than on top of the mast (report section 8.1); 262 hours of valid 10-minute averages, normalised to sea-level air density, the same density as the lesson's turbine. The report publishes bins, not the individual 10-minute points. The spread drawn on the page is one standard deviation of the 10-minute averages in a bin, recovered as Category A uncertainty x sqrt(number of data sets), because the report's Category A uncertainty is that standard deviation divided by sqrt(N) (IEC 61400-12-1, Annex E). Below about 3 m/s the idle turbine draws a few kW for its controls, so those bins are slightly negative.
measured.cleanAbout: The clean curve drawn beside the measurements is built the lesson's way for this turbine: no output below cutIn (3 m/s, where the measured output turns positive; the report states no cut-in speed) or above cutOut; otherwise 1/2 x airDensity x rotor area x v^3 x cpBest, capped at ratedKW. cpBest = 0.52 is the highest binned power coefficient in the report's Table 6 (at 7.04 m/s).
